profile_text.body:
Khosla Ventures is a for-profit firm founded in 2004 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Its site describes it as investing in the company best positioned to harness AI's exponential advances to build beneficial, human-aligned intelligence, and it refers to leveraging tailwinds, proprietary data and AI talent to build a finance workflow platform.

Much of the material on the site is commentary on AI and economics rather than a description of the firm. It asserts that AI will make expertise near free and that the labor portion of the economy will decline sharply relative to capital, and it raises the question of eliminating preferential treatment of capital gains tax, citing a figure of 40% of capital gains taxes paid by a group the excerpt does not name. It also states that the business model of elite universities is poised to collapse when the return on a $300,000 law or medical degree evaporates, and asks who will build the first billion dollar revenue company with fewer than 100 employees.

The facts held on the company list no products and no MCP servers, and no individual lawsuits. Its litigation record shows a count of 281 legal matters in California.
